Foundations should NOT rest on:
questions.n: Foundations must rest on stable, natural soil or engineered piles. Standard earth fill is prone to settlement.

questions.q: Your client asks you to erect a commercial building on land that was formerly a rice field. On what type of soil should the foundation rest?
questions.n: Rice fields consist of topsoil and soft silt. For a commercial building, you must excavate until you reach 'Hard' or stable strata.

questions.q: A structural member that functions to transfer building loads safely into the ground is called a:
questions.n: Footings are the specific base elements that distribute loads to the soil.

questions.q: What do you call the underlying structure that forms the foundation of a building or other structure?
questions.n: Substructure refers to all parts of the building below the ground level, including the foundation.

questions.q: The isolated footing of residential houses usually rests on:
questions.n: Gravel provides a level, drainage-ready surface for the concrete footing to sit on.
